verdicts.strongest_argument: Both legs of this claim are in one document that the capture stored in full, and the larger leg is not a footnote the hunter dug out - it is the company's own headline bullet. The 2026-05-29 Q1 6-K (docs/3f571c7cb5d3488b30b59c9d455ca60bcbbfc75a.txt, item 3 of snapshots/20260904T154434Z.json) leads its highlights with 'Adjusted Net Income of $12.4 million and Adjusted Earnings per common unit (basic and diluted) of $0.29' against GAAP $17.4m / $0.43, and Appendix B footnote (2) says the excluded item 'Includes other income from insurance claims for damages incurred in prior years' against the $4,893k 'Other income' line. So Dynagas itself published, three months before this print, that $0.14 of the $0.43 was non-recurring insurance - the hunter's $0.13 is the company's own number, restated. The market's response to that release was +0.27% (baseline history 2026-05-29), i.e. it never capitalised the insurance gain, so there is nothing to give back when it does not repeat. The Clean Energy gap is in the same release, in plain CEO commentary: 'redelivered from her previous charter with SEFE in early April 2026 and was successfully delivered under her new time charter with Rio Grande at the end of April 2026.' What the corpus does not contain is anyone multiplying ~25 days by the disclosed $69,360/day average hire (~$1.7m, ~1.2% of the $137.9m cap in event.json), and it does not contain the two third-party summaries that would have done so - the TipRanks and StockTitan Q1 pieces are both in the sweep's 'skipped' list with fetch failures. That unconnected arithmetic on one vessel of six is the only genuinely new part, and it is small. Separately, the cash-return content of this print was already out: the $0.050 per common unit distribution for the quarter ended June 30 2026 was declared 2026-08-13 and the 6-K body is stored at docs/5d5ab7f71f81bc72e75bcdd0035a7e053fa66928.txt, unchanged from prior quarters, on a +1.58% day.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Company reports Q1 Adjusted Net Income $12.4m / Adjusted EPS $0.29 against GAAP $0.43, with Other income of $4,893k footnoted as insurance claims for prior-year damages, and CEO commentary dating the Clean Energy redelivery to early April and its Rio Grande delivery to end-April 2026.
Declares the $0.050 per common unit distribution for the quarter ended June 30 2026 - the quarter now being reported - four weeks before the print.
Third-party summary of the FY2025 6-K already framing utilisation decay and off-hire from unscheduled repairs as the story on this name.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json (capture) runs 2026-06-08 to a partial 2026-09-04 bar and shows no directional move attributable to the Q1 disclosure window; the baseline records the 2026-05-29 print itself at +0.27%, so the insurance gain was never priced in and its absence is not a new negative. Spot 3.86 on 2026-09-08 with run_up_5d 0.0 and run_up_20d +0.26% - flat, which is consistent with the hunter's reading that nothing has been marked, but also with a market that already discounted a one-off it never paid for. Median historical reaction 1.14%, max 6.47%, so the tape's own priors cap what any earnings-quality claim on this name is worth.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A captured third-party estimate or preview that carried the $0.43 GAAP figure forward as the Q2 bar - i.e. evidence that someone was actually anchored on the un-adjusted number - would move this down toward 35.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The September-November 2026 commencement window is published twice inside this capture, in two independently stored bodies: the maritimes.gr syndication of the original 2023-07-13 GlobeNewswire release (docs/2f55a33d0047c5903f3e135afdcc25a7a0443648.txt, line 1063) and offshore-energy.biz's trade write-up of the same charters (docs/575db7651cbf1d9181b9565adb71d492d22a1f88.txt, line 376), both retrieved as items 4 and 5 of snapshots/20260904T154434Z.json. The Equinor revenue weight is published too, in a third body: StockTitan's 20-F summary states 'In 2025, SEFE accounted for 40% of total operating revenues, Yamal 35% and Equinor 25%' (docs/384edcd1a87ec9ed554b05d4a66847f353de315c.txt line 1763). So every component is in the corpus, and a charter-expiry schedule on a six-ship MLP with three charterers is the most structural fact about the name - age is not novelty. Two mechanism problems are worse for the claim than the publication question. First, event.json gives fiscal_quarter_ending Jun/2026: a September-November handover cannot touch the numbers in this print at all, so the channel is commentary only and the company gives no guidance. Second, the same Q1 release the hunter's other finding relies on states 'estimated contracted time charter coverage for 100%, 100%, and 65% of its fleet estimated Available Days for 2026, 2027, and 2028' as of 2026-05-29 - the company's own published coverage leaves essentially no uncontracted 2026 days for a three-to-four-week unpaid window to sit in. The claim has to argue that number is wrong, and the corpus does not contain that argument.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Arctic Aurora fixed to Rio Grande for about seven years 'commencing between September - November 2026 following the expiration of the existing Time Charter to Equinor ASA'.
Independent trade press repeats the same September-November 2026 Arctic Aurora commencement window and the ~$270m backlog addition.
Publishes the charterer concentration the claim rests on - SEFE 40%, Yamal 35%, Equinor 25% of 2025 revenue - in third-party summary form.
Company states contracted coverage of 100% of estimated Available Days for 2026 and 100% for 2027 as of 2026-05-29, which cuts against a material unpaid handover gap inside 2026.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No move to point at either way: run_up_5d 0.0, run_up_20d +0.26%, spot 3.86, and the capture's bars from 2026-06-08 through the partial 2026-09-04 print trade in a 3.32-3.90 band with no break around any date the transition became discussable. That flatness is the hunter's own argument, but it is equally consistent with a fact three years old and outside the reported quarter. avg_volume_20d 50,675 on a $138m cap means the tape cannot be expected to encode a Q4 commentary item at all.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A captured document showing the Arctic Aurora handover already begun with idle days inside the June quarter, or the company withdrawing the 100% 2026 coverage figure, would move this below 30.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Two of the three date moves are in the captured wire copy, not merely reachable: the corrected announcement is stored in full at docs/8af3cf4d176d302876cb3e430c3ccbf0f6cbda16.txt (item 1 of snapshots/20260904T154434Z.json), a Manila Times syndication of the GlobeNewswire release dated 2026-09-03 carrying the verbatim text 'before market opens in New York on Tuesday, September 8, 2026'. Both original GlobeNewswire URLs and both StockTitan versions are additionally logged in that snapshot's 'skipped' list, so the capture proves at least five distinct publications of the date announcements. The first release's error is also self-explaining rather than a friction tell: September 7 2026 was Labor Day, so 'after the close on Monday September 7' was a clerical slip that any wire desk corrects the next morning, which is exactly what happened. The third slip - the results 6-K accepted 2026-09-09 05:24 ET - is not in the pre-print corpus at all; it comes from seal.json, whose accession postdates the last DLNG sweep of 2026-09-04, so I cannot treat it as something the market could have read before the print, and I decline to score it as either priced or unpriced. On magnitude the claim is self-limiting: a one-day results slip on a nano-cap with no consensus is worth close to nothing, and the tape agrees - across the three sessions after the first announcement (09-01 77,700, 09-02 49,200, 09-03 35,800 shares against avg_volume_20d 50,675) volume is unremarkable and the close round-trips 3.86 to 3.70 and back to 3.86 by 09-08.

The superseded first date announcement, publicly on the wire and captured as a URL.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The bars around the announcements show nothing: closes 3.86 (08-31), 3.79, 3.76, 3.70 on 09-01 to 09-03 and back to 3.86 by 2026-09-08 per the baseline's spot, with run_up_5d exactly 0.0. Volume on the announcement days sits at or below the 50,675 twenty-day average. If a thrice-moved date were a friction signal, this is where it would show, and it does not - which cuts both ways but caps the size at essentially zero.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A captured pre-print document showing the September 8 release failed to appear - i.e. the slip becoming public before the print rather than only via the filing stamp - plus some hard news attached to it, would move this to the 25-35 band.

interactions: DLNG#0 and DLNG#1 both rest on docs/3f571c7cb5d3488b30b59c9d455ca60bcbbfc75a.txt, the 2026-05-29 Q1 6-K, and the document cuts opposite ways for them: it supplies #0's off-hire and insurance facts while its 100%/100% contracted-coverage statement for 2026-2027 argues against #1's premise of a material unpaid 2026 handover window. #0 and #1 also share the Clean Energy handover as their only precedent for the cost of a charter transition, so they are not two independent observations of off-hire risk but one observation used twice. DLNG#2's third slip is the only element in this brief whose evidence (seal.json) postdates the capture's last sweep.
corpus_limits: docs/3b91788ea2d775cdc6ce375ac9d5c19364905ce2.txt (stocktwits DLNG sentiment) carries non-empty tripwire_tells for post-earnings and beat-consensus language and was excluded in both directions. Eighteen URLs in snapshots/20260904T154434Z.json failed to fetch, including both GlobeNewswire date releases, the TipRanks and StockTitan Q1 summaries, the Seeking Alpha 2027 Yamal piece and every consensus/price-target source - so I cannot test whether any third-party preview netted the Clean Energy idle days against the higher Rio Grande rate, and cannot verify what estimate the single analyst in event.json carried. quote.json in the capture ends on a partial 2026-09-04 bar (3.6101, fetched intraday 15:55 UTC), so no 09-04 close and no 09-08 bar exist in the capture; I used the baseline's 2026-09-08 spot of 3.86 for the run-in and used no 2026-09-09 bar anywhere.
